question: Archaeological evidence of which of the following dance forms dating back to the 2nd century BC was found in the caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Odissi** is the dance form for which archaeological evidence dating back to the 2nd century BC was found in the caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri.
 
• The **Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves** are located in the Indian state of Odisha and are known for their historical and religious significance.
 
• These caves were carved out as residential blocks for Jain monks during the reign of King Kharavela.
 
• Odissi is one of the **eight classical dance forms of India** and originates from the state of Odisha.
 
• The dance is characterized by its intricate movements, expressions, and poses, often depicting religious stories and spiritual themes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi** is traditionally a dance-drama genre of performance art, known for its grace and fluidity.
 
• It is performed predominantly by women, though there is also a male version called **Gotipua**.
 
• Odissi music is based on classical ragas and talas, and the dance is performed in temples as well as on stage.
 
• The dance form has a rich history and has been preserved through generations by the **Maharis** (temple dancers) and **Gotipuas** (young boys dressed as girls).
 
• Odissi has been recognized as a classical dance form of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
